name: La Rothière
summary: Three days after Brienne, Blücher, joined by much of Schwarzenberg's army, came on at noon against Napoleon's army strung out over seven miles of villages from Dienville to Morvilliers, the gaps between them held by cavalry, in falling snow that made the roads mud and the guns almost useless. Sacken's Russians attacked La Rothière in the centre and took it with the bayonet, as Nansouty's Guard cavalry was broken in front of it; Gérard held Dienville against Gyulai's Austrians, but the Crown Prince of Württemberg took La Giberie and Petit-Mesnil and Wrede took Chaumesnil. Rothembourg's Young Guard retook La Rothière twice in the evening before being driven out, and under cover of the storm the French drew off towards Lesmont, leaving some fifty guns: Napoleon's first defeat on French soil.

forces.name: Dufour's Division
forces.formation: 1st Division, Paris Reserve (Gérard), with Piquet's cavalry
forces.summary: Gérard's division on the far right, holding Dienville and its bridge over the Aube. Gyulai's Austrians took the bridge and lost it again, and attacked the village from both banks in turn; Gérard held it until the army drew off, and gave it up only at midnight. Piquet's cavalry stood to its left, towards La Rothière.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for La Rothière, from Koch's and Damitz's histories of the campaign and the French archives.
Battalion numbers and brigades his La Rothière return leaves out are from his return of 25 January, a week before.

Its battalions were from the depots of a dozen regiments, mostly one from each, put together in brigades that winter; each is shown as a regiment of its one battalion. The 113th, raised in Tuscany, was the one whole regiment.

Piquet's brigade, the cavalry of Gérard's wing, is with the division here. The Gardes d'Honneur, raised in 1813 from young men of means who equipped themselves and rode dressed as hussars, are the list's Hussars.
Nafziger gives the division's artillery as three hundred gunners and train, shown as one foot battery.
Jarry's four regiments and Bellair's five, where the list's brigade takes three, and four light battalions, where it allows one light regiment in the division, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Ricard's Division
forces.summary: The remnant of Ricard's division of 1813, lent from Marmont's corps to Gérard, which stood with Dufour's round Dienville on the right through the Austrian attacks.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for La Rothière, from Koch's and Damitz's histories of the campaign and the French archives.

Its thirteen battalions were what was left of whole regiments after Leipzig, a hundred to six hundred men each; on 25 January the division counted 2,300 men. They are shown at full size; the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.

Nafziger gives the battalions as one brigade under Fournier and Boudin together. They are split between them here, the light battalions and the 40th and 50th Line with Fournier and the regiments raised in 1813 with Boudin, as Wikipedia's order of battle, after Nafziger's history, has them.

Fournier's seven regiments and Boudin's five, where the list's brigade takes three, and five light battalions, where it allows one light regiment in the division, show as historical departures. Nafziger gives the division no guns.

forces.name: Duhesme's Division
forces.summary: The one division of Victor's corps in the centre, with a brigade in La Rothière itself and the other behind it. At four Sacken's Russians came on with the bayonet, their muskets wet with snow; after a hard fight Duhesme's men were driven out, but some held on in the houses at the north end, and Colbert's Guard cavalry threw back every attempt to come out of the village.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for La Rothière, from Koch's and Damitz's histories of the campaign and the French archives.
Each regiment had a single battalion; each is shown as its one battalion. Its brigades and battery are as at Brienne, from his return of 25 January: Nafziger's La Rothière return gives none.
Nafziger gives the II Corps' batteries together, not by division: four 6-pdr foot batteries, a 12-pdr battery and three horse batteries. One of the 6-pdr foot batteries is with each division here.
Its foot battery, with four battalions where the list wants six for one, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Nansouty's Guard Cavalry
forces.formation: Colbert's, Lefebvre-Desnouettes's and Guyot's divisions, Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: The Guard horse, between La Rothière and Petit-Mesnil in the centre. Its first charge was beaten back by Sacken's guns; its second drove off Lanskoy's hussars, but as it came on the Russian infantry it was struck by Panchulidzev's dragoons and broken, losing the Guard's horse batteries. In the evening Colbert's squadrons held the Russians in La Rothière, and Guyot's rode with Meunier's division against Chaumesnil.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for La Rothière, from Koch's and Damitz's histories of the campaign and the French archives.

Nafziger gives Colbert's and Lefebvre-Desnouettes's divisions with squadrons of the same regiments, and Guyot's service squadrons drawn from both; each regiment's squadrons are shown together as one unit, as at Hanau. The three divisions had about two thousand men.
Nansouty, who commanded the Guard cavalry, is from Wikipedia's account; Nafziger gives the divisions on their own.
Two horse batteries, one with each division, are here; the Guard lost twenty-four horse guns in the fight.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Milhaud's Cavalry
forces.summary: Grouchy's horsemen, posted between Petit-Mesnil and Chaumesnil to fill the gap between Victor's villages and Marmont's. As the Crown Prince of Württemberg's corps took La Giberie and Petit-Mesnil and Wrede's cavalry came round past the French squares, they could not hold the open ground against the allied horse.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Piré's 9th Light Cavalry Division is the two light brigades, Briche's 5th Heavy Division Montélégier's and Ludot's dragoons, and L'Héritier's 6th Heavy Division Lamotte's and Collaert's.
Its regiments were weak, about two hundred men each; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit many of them.

forces.name: Lagrange's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's infantry on the left wing, in Morvilliers, with a battalion out east at La Chaise. Wrede's Austrians and Bavarians cleared it out of La Chaise and the Bois d'Ajou in the afternoon and took Chaumesnil on its right; Marmont held Morvilliers into the night and covered the army's retreat.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for La Rothière, from Koch's and Damitz's histories of the campaign and the French archives.
Battalion numbers and brigades his La Rothière return leaves out are from his return of 25 January, a week before.
Its marine regiments were sailors and naval gunners of the fleet's artillery, brought inland in 1813; they fought well, and are shown as Line, the list's Veteran upgrade would suit them.

Nafziger gives the division as one brigade under Joubert and Pelleport, with Lefol's division taken into it. Its regiments are brigaded here as Wikipedia's order of battle, after Nafziger's history, has them: Joubert's and Pelleport's of Lagrange's own division, and the two of Lefol's, the first of which has no known commander.
Nafziger gives the 37th Line, but it is the 37th Léger, which served in the division at Leipzig; the 37th Line was in Duhesme's division.
Its battalions were very weak: the division had 4,600 men in twenty-one battalions. They are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.

Marmont's artillery is from the 25 January return: three companies of the 3rd Foot Artillery, one with the division and two in the corps artillery, as the list takes them. Clavel's four regiments, where the list's brigade takes three, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Rothembourg's Division
forces.summary: Ney's nearest Young Guard division, called up from Brienne-la-Vieille. As the army made ready to withdraw, Napoleon sent it to retake La Rothière: its first brigade took the village and was thrown out by Olsufiev's Russians, and its second took it again before Grimmer's Austrians and Paskevich's grenadiers drove it out. It re-formed north of the village at eight, and covered the retreat in the snowstorm.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for La Rothière, from Koch's and Damitz's histories of the campaign and the French archives.
Its regiments were newly raised that winter, largely of conscripts under a cadre of veterans; they are the list's Young Guard, as it rates them.
Each regiment had two battalions of about four hundred men; they are shown at full size.
Nafziger gives the division without its brigades; its six regiments are split between two here, in his order. The Flanqueurs-Chasseurs, the Young Guard's light infantry, are the list's Tirailleurs.
Its two foot companies are one battery with each brigade.

forces.summary: Twelve thousand Austrian infantry on the allied left, which came into action only at four. Fresnel's division crossed the Aube to attack Dienville and its bridge from the west bank and was thrown back, and Hohenlohe's attacked from the east bank and was repulsed; Gyulai's 12-pdrs bombarded the village, and Grimmer's brigade was sent to help at La Rothière. notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Austrian 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.

The Mariassy and Ignaz Gyulai regiments, recruited in Hungary, are the list's Hungarian infantry.

Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.
